channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Swiss Franc holds ground following domestic Producer and Import Prices data
item.description: USD/CHF depreciates after three days of gains, trading around 0.8130 during the European hours on Thursday. The pair holds losses as the Swiss Franc (CHF) remains stronger following Swiss Producer and Import Prices data for July.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ hike expectations support JPY against US Dollar - MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes the Japanese Yen has strengthened modestly as markets anticipate a faster pace of Bank of Japan policy tightening.

item.title: Eurozone Industrial Production remains flat in June vs. -0.1% estimates
item.description: The Eurozone industrial sector activity remained flat in June, while it was expected to decline 0.1%, according to data published by Eurostat. In May, Industrial production contracted by 0.3%, revised lower from -0.2%.

item.title: Euro bounces off one-week low, holds above 1.1500 vs USD as traders look to US PPI
item.description: The EUR/USD pair drops to a one-and-a-half-week low during the first half of the European session, though it manages to recover a few pips from the vicinity of the 1.1500 psychological mark.

item.title: Indian Rupee falls as US Dollar holds gains
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) opens on a cautious note against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday due to overnight gains in the latter. The USD/INR pair edges up to near 95.42 after a corrective move the previous day, as fears of a prolonged global energy supply disruption have strengthened the US Dollar.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Recovery not just about Oil – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Michael Pfister argues Canada’s recent economic improvement is not solely driven by higher Oil and gas prices linked to the Iran conflict.

item.title: Euro advances against Canadian Dollar amid ECB hawkish stance, lower oil prices
item.description: EUR/CAD halts its six-day losing streak, trading around 1.6080 during the European hours on Thursday. The currency cross gains ground as the Euro (EUR) receives support as the macroeconomic picture in the Eurozone continues to support the European Central Bank's (ECB) hawkish stance.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Cooling NZ inflation expectations push Kiwi under pressure
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) underperforms its major currency peers, trading 0.45% down at around 0.5830 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Thursday.

item.title: US Dollar: Markets remain hawkish after CPI – ING
item.description: ING strategists Francesco Pesole, Frantisek Taborsky and Chris Turner note that the Dollar strengthened after an in-line US CPI, as markets had positioned for a hotter print.

item.title: Indian Rupee: RBI seen delaying rate hikes – MUFG
item.description: Michael Wan at MUFG reports that India’s July Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose to 4.45% year-on-year, slightly below consensus but above June’s 4.38%, driven mainly by higher food prices.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Upside risk intact above 0.7025 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report AUD/USD briefly broke above 0.7075 to 0.7091 before retreating to close almost unchanged at 0.7063.

item.title: Dow Jones futures rise as cooling inflation reduces Fed rate hike bets
item.description: Dow Jones futures gain 0.08% to trade around 53,910 during European hours on Thursday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures rise by 0.09% to trade around 7,780 and Nasdaq 100 futures advance 0.06%, trading near 29,870.

item.title: Gold languishes near daily low; eyes $4,350 amid Fed hike bets, USD strength
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) retreats over $100 from its highest level since June 5, touched earlier this Thursday, and maintains its bearish tone around the $4,375-$4,370 region through the first half of the European session.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Soft profile sustained on SNB stance – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that the Swiss Franc (CHF) has weakened toward their year-end EUR/CHF target of 0.94, making it a preferred funding currency for carry trades.

item.title: Norwegian Krone: Dovish risks but bullish view against Euro – ING
item.description: Francesco Pesole at ING sees some downside risks for the Norwegian Krone from Norges Bank’s meeting, as benign CPI‑ATE prints could tilt communication slightly less hawkish. He still expects rates to stay at 4.25% today and another hike later this year, but is less convinced about multiple moves.

item.title: Japanese Yen holds ground due to potential intervention from Japanese authorities
item.description: USD/JPY inches lower after registering minor losses in the previous day, trading around 159.40 during the European hours on Thursday. The currency pair hovers near the crucial 160.00 level, keeping traders on high alert for possible intervention from Japanese authorities.

item.title: Russian Ruble: Trade boost from Oil seen fading – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose reports Russia’s June merchandise trade surplus rose to USD 12.5bn, up over 50% year-on-year, as higher Oil prices and improved Urals pricing supported exports.

item.title: US Dollar Index Price Forecast: DXY bulls await trading range breakout above 100.00
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback against a basket of currencies, is seen building on the previous day's sold bounce from the post-CPI swing low and prolonging its weekly uptrend for the fourth straight day.

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: Prolonged energy supply concerns remain key tailwind
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), futures on NYMEX, trades 0.5% higher at around $82.10 during the European trading session on Thursday. The oil price reflects strength as fears of a prolonged energy supply disruption continue to act as a key tailwind for oil prices.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed-driven hedge rebuilding revives selling pressure – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu argues that the July Fed meeting marked a peak in Dollar dehedging rather than an end to U.S. exceptionalism. Cross-border investors are rebuilding USD hedges, reducing effective unhedged U.S. exposure while maintaining broadly solid underlying demand for U.S. assets.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar stabilizes ahead of next batch of US data
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Thursday, August 13:

item.title: British Pound: Upside capped near 1.3555 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note GBP/USD briefly traded above 1.3535 to 1.3540 before slipping back to close at 1.3496. Intraday, the pair is seen range-trading between 1.3475 and 1.3525.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah remains subdued as safe-haven demand lifts US Dollar
item.description: USD/IDR gains ground for the third consecutive day, trading around 17,920 during the early European hours on Thursday. The pair appreciates as the US Dollar (USD) recovers its daily losses amid escalating geopolitical tensions between the US and Iran.

item.title: Gold: Upside capped by Fed hike risks – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Bart Melek notes Gold extended gains after the July Consumer Price Index (CPI) matched expectations, reinforcing a dovish narrative around Fed Chair Warsh.

item.title: Canadian Dollar extends pullback from two-month high as oil-driven Fed hike bets lift USD
item.description: The USD/CAD pair builds on the previous day's bounce from the 1.3900 neighborhood, or a two-month low, and gains follow-through positive traction for the second straight day on Thursday.

item.title: Equities: AI rally and CPI relief lift US stocks – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists highlight that the S&P 500 closed just below its record high as US CPI data reduced urgency for further Federal Reserve hikes. Front-end Treasuries rallied and semiconductor strength supported equities, while volatility fell to its lowest level since January.

item.title: Euro holds gains against British Pound as UK GDP slows in Q2
item.description: The EUR/GBP cross holds positive ground near 0.8540 during the early European trading hours on Thursday. The British Pound (GBP) remains weak against the Euro (EUR) following the UK economic data.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Contained inflation supports RBI pause – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s FX team notes India’s July CPI rose slightly to 4.5% year-on-year but stayed within the Reserve Bank of India’s target band, with core inflation steady at 3.9%.

item.title: British Pound drifts away from 1.3500 as UK GDP slows down and Industrial Production falls
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) treads water against the US Dollar (USD), trading practically flat, a few pips below the 1.3500 level on Thursday's early London session.

item.title: Oil: Supply disruptions raise deficit risks – ING
item.description: ING analysts Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey note Oil prices have eased, with Brent crude ending largely flat as US-Iran talks remain in deadlock and Russian port infrastructure escapes major damage.
